exposure: longer birth hospitalization length of stay
longer index RSV hospitalization length of stay
intensive care unit admission for the index hospitalization
outcome: subsequent medically attended lower respiratory tract infection (MA LRTI) hospitalization
subsequent MA LRTI emergency department visit
subsequent MA LRTI physician office visit
cohort: The study participants were 20,181 infants who experienced an RSV hospitalization (index hospitalization) during infancy.
finding: Of the infants who experienced an RSV hospitalization, 15% had at least one subsequent medically attended lower respiratory tract infection within the same RSV season, with factors such as younger maternal age, cesarean delivery, lower birth weight, and lower gestational age increasing this risk.
mod_finding: Cesarean delivery was identified as a factor associated with an increased risk of subsequent medically attended lower respiratory tract infection.
birth_weight: Lower birth weight was measured and identified as a risk factor for subsequent MA-LRTI.
gest_age: Lower gestational age was measured and identified as a risk factor for subsequent MA-LRTI.
